page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. Three paragraphs of Scripture quotations with references, two bare section numbers, and a final paragraph ending mid-word at the foot of the column. No marginal notes or footnotes.

main_text.p: quærebat? at vos animis cavete[?],ne in vestra juventutis uxores agatur perfide. Qui odit, repudiet, inquit Iova Deus Israelitarum: & tegat iniquitatem veste sua, inquit armipotens Iova: & cavete animis, ne perfidè agatis. Malach. 2.

Congrediar autè vobiscum judicio, e-roq; celer testis in præstigiatores, in adulteros, in perjuros, in eos quì mercede fraudant mercenarios, qui viduas, qui pupillos, qui peregrinos labefactant, neque me timent, inquit armipotens Iova. Malach. 3.

p.i: Tu ergo, nate[?], corpus tuum ab omni fœditate & impudicitia tuere, L. neve committito ut omissa uxore tua flagitium admittas: H. & uxorem ducito de cognatione tua, non ullius generis, quod à majorum tuorum stirpe sit alienum. Nos enim de vatum progenie sumus. Memoria repete, fili, Abrahamum, Isa-cum,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the mark after "cavete" and after "nate" is a printed sign (a curved stroke, possibly a tilde or abbreviation) that I could not identify, so both are marked [?]. "e-roq;" is uncertain and marked [?]. The final word is broken across the line as "Isa-" / "cum," and is given with the printed hyphen. Long s is plain s throughout. The "L." and "H." before "neve" and "uxorem" are printed inline section letters, kept in the text.
